newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African budget passes first hurdle.
newsitem.headline: S.African budget passes first hurdle.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's 186.7 billion rand budget for fiscal 1997/98 passed its first hurdle in the National Assembly on Thursday.
Legislators voted 287 to 10 for adoption of the budget at the end of a "first reading" debate, but will vote again around mid-year after all the ministers have defended their spending plans.
The budget was opposed by the white separatist Freedom Front, which holds nine of the 400 National Assembly seats, and by the liberal Democratic Party, with seven seats.
Manuel's budget, the first to be prepared and presented by a member of President Nelson Mandela's ruling African National Congress, was welcomed by business and investors.
Manuel reduced government spending in real terms and budgeted for a deficit of four percent, down from 5.1 percent in the year to March 31.
